programme.title: Simon King's Shetland Adventure
programme.desc: Spring brings an influx of wildlife to the islands, where the former Springwatch presenter is living for a year. Exploring the sea, Simon discovers starfish, moon jellyfish and gets close to a seal. He also follows the struggle at a wildlife sanctuary to teach an injured otter cub to use its back legs, and gives his daughter Savannah a lesson in birdwatching

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Meet the big birds, a feathered family who've never flown a day in their lives. From ostriches to kiwis, these bizarre birds appear to be nature's greatest novelty act. How they came to be and how they continue to survive is a fascinating tale that has long captivated David Attenborough. In this programme, he tells a story of dedicated dads, enormous eggs and a serious need for speed. And far from being the court jesters of the animal world, these flightless curiosities once nearly ruled the planet

programme.title: Paris Police 1910
programme.desc: As Jouin quietly continues his investigation into Julien Fiersi, Labruyere teaches Hutin some golden rules about journalism, and Meg Steinheil is warned that there is a thief in her household. Weidmann is both incredulous and furious that Jeanne Chauvin has agreed to take on the notorious Madame Stenheil as a client. In French

programme.title: Paris Police 1910
programme.desc: Jouin and Cochefert suspect Joseph Fiersi after the death of Irma Barbet and are concerned that he will kill again. programme.title: Scrublands

programme.title: Scrublands
programme.desc: After a mass poisoning at Hummingbird Beach leaves Mandy in critical condition, Martin and Uncle Vern reconcile their differences. Their renewed bond helps Martin trust his own instincts, leading him to discover evidence that clears Mandy's name and reveals Jasper's killer

programme.title: Organ Stops: Saving the King of Instruments
programme.desc: Documentary following the tireless efforts of a small band of enthusiasts to save, restore and rehome rare pipe organs that would otherwise be destroyed. Martin Renshaw dedicates his life to travelling the UK on organ rescue missions, sound engineer Marc Ogier rebuilds instruments in his back bedroom from pipes bought online, organ builder Dominic Gwynn resuscitates historical pieces that are close to death, and avant-garde musician Claire Singer uses pipe organs to create a new kind of acoustic sound

programme.title: Simon King's Shetland Adventure

programme.title: The Riviera: A History in Pictures
programme.desc: Part one of two. Actor Richard E Grant follows in the footsteps of artists who lived and painted on France's Cote d'Azur, renowned for its sunny climate. The first edition focuses on the relationship between modern art and the location's development as an international tourist haven. Cezanne, Monet and Renoir were captivated by the light and colour of the landscape in the 19th century and their resultant work advertised the region's beauty. Meanwhile, the area's vivid hues inspired Henri Matisse to adopt a new palette that set modern art on the route to abstraction

programme.title: A Stitch in Time
programme.desc: Amber Butchart combines biography, art and the history of fashion to explores the lives of historical figures through the clothes they wore, starting with Charles II

programme.title: Lesley Garrett at the BBC
programme.desc: A tribute to the voice and career of soprano Lesley Garrett, who shares her memories of some of her finest performances from a career full of BBC moments. This collection includes popular songs such as 'Somewhere' and 'Tonight,' and showcases the versatility, artistry, and warmth that have made Lesley Garrett one of Britain's most cherished performers

programme.title: The Riviera: A History in Pictures
programme.desc: Richard E Grant concludes his exploration of the French Riviera's artistic legacy by focusing on how art and celebrity became intertwined in the early part of the 20th century. Resident artists such as Picasso and Matisse found the sun-drenched landscape ideal for experimenting with their work, and as the region became a creative hub, the likes of novelist Jean Cocteau and ballet impresario Sergei Diaghilev were drawn to the area. This artistic community also liked to party on the Cote d'Azur's beaches - a pastime that proved equally irresistible to the American multimillionaires arriving in the area on board transatlantic liners

programme.title: An Inspector Calls (2015)
programme.desc: In 1912, a detective arrives in a town where a young woman has committed suicide. Interrupting a wealthy family in the midst of a lavish party, he unravels the events that led to the woman's death - an investigation with devastating repercussions as secrets are exposed and each member of the family realises they have all unwittingly played a part. Adaptation of JB Priestley's stage play, starring David Thewlis, Miranda Richardson and Ken Stott.

programme.title: An Evening with JB Priestley
programme.desc: A 1973 programme in which the author chooses extracts from his own writing to celebrate the many things that he looked back on with pleasure. With readings by Jill Balcon

programme.title: Face to Face
programme.desc: An interview from 1960 in which the sculptor talks to John Freeman about his much-loved father, his inspirational school art teacher, and how much he hates working to commission. The interview takes place in Moore's home in Perry Green, Hertfordshire.

programme.title: Ancient Worlds
programme.desc: Archaeologist and historian Richard Miles examines the collapse of the Bronze Age 3,000 years ago, and how the civilisations of the subsequent Iron Age emerged. He explores the former Phoenician cities of Byblos and Tyre and their technological contributions, including the alphabet and deep-water sailing, before heading to Israel to learn how the Assyrian war machine affected small local powers

programme.desc: Documentary following the wildlife near a remote French village, including red squirrels, wild boar, dormice and stone martens. programme.desc: The actress explores the country's history, food and culture, beginning in Paris, where she finds out about the haute cuisine tradition of the art of the table at Alain Ducasse's restaurant Le Meurice. She also meets young chefs leading a new food scene that blends French technique with global influences, including Mory Sacko at MoSuke and Hanz Gueco at Le Cheval d'Or

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: The travellers head into Eryri National Park, and the pilgrim path leads the group to Aber Falls, one of Wales's most famous natural wonders. By day six, the route goes right past Yr Wyddfa, or Mount Snowdon, the highest mountain in England and Wales, where the group attempts to reach the summit

Andrew's story is made all the more extraordinary by the fact that, at just 23, he was diagnosed with leukaemia. programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: Sue Perkins and Mel Giedroyc present as the remaining four bakers take a deep breath and head into the semi-final of the nation's favourite baking contest. However, there's no time to marvel at how far they've come - it's Patisserie Week, and they will need to demonstrate that they have skills worthy enough to see them through to this year's final. The bakers are challenged to make a signature baklava - two types of any flavour they like, before the technical challenge demands they knock up a German Schichttorte, a cake cooked in stages under the grill to create 20 layers of different coloured sponge. Finally, the showstopper sees the semi-finalists baking non-stop to create two entremets in which they should demonstrate as many personal skills and techniques as they can

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: Three contestants remain and only one more weekend of baking stands between them and the 2014 title. Judges Paul Hollywood and Mary Berry have saved their most fiendish tests till last, as the finalists face a Signature Challenge in which they have just three hours to prove they have mastered a pastry technique that usually takes a whole day. They then have to tackle a Technical Challenge without the aid of a recipe, before rustling up a Showstopper that turns sponge, caramel, choux pastry and petits fours into a winning combination. At least Sue Perkins and Mel Giedroyc are on hand to lighten the atmosphere if it all gets too tense

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: Twelve contestants begin the battle to be named Britain's best amateur baker, facing tasks devised by judges Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood, who have created 30 new tasks to test their baking skills and creativity. Their first signature challenge is to make a Madeira cake, before they attempt to bake a frosted walnut cake in the technical. Day two of the contest sees the contestants going all out to try and impress the judges with their first showstopper, the Black Forest gateau. Mel Giedroyc and Sue Perkins present

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: With the cake week completed, and one of their number already eliminated from the competition, the 11 remaining home bakers must now prove their skill at making biscuits, a task that can be deceptively difficult, and one that has undone many a confident Bake Off contestant in the past. The opening signature challenge this week is to create 24 biscotti, Italian delicacies that must be baked twice to deliver the perfect crisp crunch. Next is Paul Hollywood's technical challenge, in which the contestants tackle Arlettes - labour-intensive, puff pastry-based treats from southwest France. Finally, for the showstopper, the judges demand bespoke edible biscuit boxes, filled with 36 biscuits of different flavours. After all three rounds have concluded, it falls to Mel Giedroyc and Sue Perkins to announce which of the bakers will be asked to leave the tent

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: The 10 remaining home-bakers must steel themselves to face the full force of Paul Hollywood's discerning eye as bread week arrives. For the signature bake, the contestants are given an hour-and-a-half to prepare quick breads with no proving - which results in creative flavours such as sweet chocolate loaves and manchego and prosciutto-stuffed bread coming to the fore. Next up is the technical challenge, in which Paul lulls the bakers into a false sense of security by asking them to make baguettes, a relatively simple task that concludes with 'the male judge' delivering one of his most brutal verdicts yet. Finally, a bicycle, a snake, a lion and even Brighton Pavilion find their way into the tent's ovens as the showstopper challenge sees the competitors crafting edible 3D bread sculptures

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: Mel Giedroyc and Sue Perkins usher the nine remaining home-bakers back into the tent for the fourth week of the contest. This time, the competitors must tackle desserts, beginning with a signature challenge in the form of a French classic - creme brulees. With the clock ticking, the contestants must grill their offerings to perfection to avoid serving up an unappetising scrambled egg and custard soup. Next up is the technical challenge, in which Mary Berry asks the group to prepare Spanische Windtorte, an Austrian meringue inspired by the tastes of Spain, Switzerland and France. Finally, the showstopper this week involves baking a three-tiered cheesecake stack, and only the most structurally sound creations will be worthy of securing their maker the title of star baker

programme.desc: The Goods begin to reap their just rewards for the hard work they have put into the garden, although Barbara is too tired and bored to appreciate the benefits. Comedy, starring Richard Briers and Felicity Kendal

programme.title: Lies, Deceit and Betrayal
programme.desc: Two couples trying to secure their retirement each find themselves at the centre of an elaborate investment scam, giving thousands of pounds to someone who doesn't seem to exist

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: Alison invites Lucy to stay, but begins to worry about her real motivations after a dire warning from her solicitor. The Captain decides to put his surveillance skills to the task of discovering whether Lucy is who she claims to be. A prank by Julian leaves Mike with an inappropriate e-mail and some awkward explaining to do with his new boss. Comedy, starring Charlotte Ritchie and Jessica Knappett

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: Alison realises that Kitty's fond memories of her sister conceal a darker truth, and tries to help her come to terms with her past. The rest of the ghosts fear that getting Kitty to open up will just be traumatic for everyone - but end up sharing some unresolved issues of their own. Mike resorts to witchcraft in a bid to see the ghosts for himself

programme.title: My Family
programme.desc: Susan and Ben visit Janey at her new university, but receive a frosty reception and decide to use the excursion as an opportunity to spice up their relationship. programme.title: My Family
programme.sub-title: The Second Greatest Story Ever Told
programme.desc: Susan attends an audition, but is outraged to land only the minor role of shepherd number two, especially when Nick manages to win the part of Jesus. programme.title: My Family
programme.desc: Michael takes a shine to classmate Bex, much to the horror of his mother Susan, who does not have a very high opinion of the girl. It seems a father-and-son chat is in order - until the Harpers realise they are starting to sound just like their own parents

programme.title: Teleshopping
programme.desc: A chance to buy goods from the comfort of home

programme.title: The Bill
programme.desc: A road traffic accident turns into a drugs investigation when a quantity of cocaine is found in the crashed vehicle. The driver is dead, but Yvonne is more interested in his passenger, none other than Shirley Moss, who's suffered two broken legs. However, when she begins to question the errant teenager about her continued involvement in drugs, Yvonne soon has reason to believe the youngster isn't the architect of her own downfall - especially after the PC's sister, Beverley, is spotted entering a dealer's flat being staked out by Ken and Suzie. Elsewhere, Mark is upset that his colleagues in SO19 have discovered he is gay, but with the secret now out he throws caution to the wind and decides to take his relationship with Lance one step further - it looks like Sun Hill is about to witness its first gay wedding. With romance in the air, the Christmas party gets into full swing, and new girl Amber certainly enjoys herself - and causes much gossip - by very publicly kissing one of the barmaids - but sadly it looks like love is off the cards for Neil when he spies lover Andrea in a passionate embrace with Smithy. Michele Austin, Ofo Uhiara, Andrew Lancel and Stefan Booth star

programme.title: The Bill
programme.desc: It's a difficult day for Yvonne as she faces up to the fact that she was wrong to throw Shirley out of the house. However, the youngster eventually accepts her apology and it looks as if, once she has pulled through this latest mishap, the kindly PC will be able to get her life back on track - until fate deals a terrible blow. Meanwhile, with the tensions in his relationship with Andrea beginning to take their toll, Neil is devastated at the news that she has been critically injured. He turns up at the hospital, only to be faced by Smithy, having already filled his shoes. Lance finally accepts Mark's proposal of marriage after a long day of deliberation, while Gina is surprised to catch a glimpse of Irene Radford. She is convinced her eyes are deceiving her - until Jack confides in her that Sun Hill's crime matriarch is indeed back. Michele Austin, Andrew Lancel, Simon Rouse, Roberta Taylor, Lynda Bellingham and Stefan Booth star

programme.title: The Bill
programme.desc: Having discovered Irene Radford is back, Gina is determined to put her old enemy behind bars once and for all - and the two are soon face to face again when an intruder at the Radford house turns out to be Irene herself, who claims she has returned because she is critically ill with cancer. However, the police have got wind that she is plotting one final raid before retiring from a life of crime for good, so Phil is tasked to monitor a prison meeting between Irene and her son David, where the top brass are hoping he'll glean valuable information about the job. Unfortunately, the philandering DS is easily distracted by an old flame working at the prison and misses half the conversation - so when the raid gets under way, it soon becomes clear they've been duped, and a senior officer ends up staring down the barrel of Irene's gun. Back at the station, Honey is upset to learn that Amber has taken the 'shy and sensitive' Steve Hunter's virginity, while Sam seems to be warming to Phil. Is romance on the cards for Sun Hill's detective sergeants? Roberta Taylor and Lynda Bellingham star

programme.title: The Bill
programme.desc: Following the Radford family's botched attempt to spring David from prison, Irene drives off with Gina at gunpoint and forces the inspector to let her colleagues know she means business. If they don't give up the chase, she won't hesitate to pull the trigger. Soon, Gina finds herself alone with her enemy, and as they begin to talk, the two of them realise they understand one another better than they could possibly have imagined. However, when Irene orders the shooting of Jack Gaunt, it becomes clear Gina is still in very real danger. Meanwhile, Honey has it out with Steve, disappointed that he had sex with Amber, and accusing him of being as bad as his brother. Indeed, Phil is having his fair share of problems as Sam discovers that his New Year's invitation followed hard on the heels of his dalliance with the prison liaison officer. Roberta Taylor, Lynda Bellingham, Lisa Maxwell and Scott Maslen star

programme.title: The Bill

programme.title: The Supervet

programme.title: The Supervet

programme.title: The Supervet
